One hit runs in a fixed order: crit roll sets the camera jolt and rumble (enemy targets only), the floating number is added before HP changes, then damage, then the hit sound (gated by a per-creature cooldown) and the hit state (crit bypasses poise, cooldown and stun gate the state). Read in Entity.cpp takeHit 319-710, receipts in receipts.tsv.

Knockback is a per-frame speed from a power post-effect (magnitude over frame cap), one knockback active at a time (a second one is dropped), moves the target through the collision grid, and blocks the target's own walking while it runs. Transferable as one lock per target window for three-on-one.

Camera jolt is a random per-axis offset within a fixed strength, for a timer set by a crit on an enemy or by shakycam map events (21 event lines in the data pack). Jolt is client-only; keep it out of src/fight and use a seeded client RNG.

Floating combat numbers use one colour per type (crit, taken, given, miss, buff) and push older labels up when they overlap (CombatText.cpp 179-190). This is the readability rule that keeps a three-attacker fight legible at 375 wide.

No hit-stop (freeze frame) and no screen flash for hits in the engine half read; grep of src for shake, freeze, pause and flash found only the shake and rumble. Do not claim a hit-stop donor from this repo. Paired data pack read by count (20 sfx_hit, 13 force or knockback post-effects, 2 cooldown_hit lines).
